results.reason: Request.confirm_digest() is the first 12 hex characters of sha256 over method, url and body. The created, modified and last_used fields are removed first, including inside JSON-string bodies such as save-journey's document_data. Every dry run now returns 'confirm'. perform_write requires --confirm with --yes and recomputes the digest just before sending. A missing or different digest raises UsageError (exit 2) and sends nothing. The error shows the request it would send now and the confirm value the user passed. It deliberately never prints the expected digest, so an agent cannot copy it out of the error. The previously approved request cannot be shown because only its digest exists; it lives in the chat. build_plan.py adds 'confirm' to WRITE_IN_YES (which also creates the --confirm CLI option) and to the DRY_RUN output schema. It also updates the ROUND_TRIP, APPROVAL and plan.md Writes text. render_skill.py's Writes section now tells the agent to run --yes --confirm <confirm> and to redo the dry run after a refusal. I updated existing test helpers (run_write, sent_write, the bus-stop favourite test) to take confirm from a dry run first, which is the new contract. No assertion was changed or removed. PENDING-APPROVALS.md still shows --yes calls without --confirm and is outside my partition.

results.reason: The defect was still there at transport.py:86 (follow_redirects=True on the client). Every request now goes out with follow_redirects=False and Transport handles 3xx itself. A redirect is followed only for a read GET, only when the target has the same origin as the endpoint host, and only up to MAX_REDIRECTS=5. Each followed hop gets its own pacer turn and its own log line (class "Redirect"). A redirect to another host, any redirect on a POST/PUT/DELETE or GET write, and a sixth hop are logged and raised as ContractBroken (exit 14) before anything is sent to the new location. I chose same origin, which is stricter than the proposed two-host allowlist. That means a citymapper.com endpoint redirecting to turnstile-api (or the reverse) is refused. Behaviour change and risk: a POST read (searchpost, journeytimes, refreshjourneys) that gets a 3xx now fails with ContractBroken instead of httpx following it. A signed-in GET redirected on the same origin now carries Cookie on the next hop, where httpx used to drop it. The documented same-origin line-page redirect (/{region}/l/{alias}) is still followed.

review.notes:
I found 9 rule breaks: 5 command-input changes and 4 style issues. None of the changes breaks the endpoint, live-request, pacing, secret or test-loosening rules.

Checks I ran:
- Offline suite (`uv run --offline python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider`): "499 passed in 1.11s". conftest blocks the real network.
- Provenance gate (`uv run --offline python scripts/check_provenance.py`): "positive control: 8 of 8 planted source defects and 3 of 3 planted objects caught", "Endpoint 35, PendingEndpoint 22, ALL_ENDPOINTS 57", "provenance violations: 0". No new endpoint literals were added. endpoints.py only gained `writes=True` on createtripurl and createshorturl, and the gate itself was strengthened, not loosened.
- No live requests: var/logs/requests-2026-10-10.jsonl has 64 lines and none at or after 09:27. The last write to it was 09:24, before this run.
- No pacing constants changed. pacing.py now persists the fail-closed halt, which is stricter.
- No password login, no cookie on argv, and no secret printed in outputs, errors or logs. Dry-run describe() excludes headers.
- No existing test was deleted or weakened. support.schema_errors now also rejects undeclared keys, which is stronger. Edits to existing tests only adapt them to the new --confirm and --use-web-session-id inputs.
- Across all 36 files: no em dashes, emojis, tabs, non-3-space indentation or trailing blank line at EOF.

Things I could not verify from the files:
- The bite proofs, because no bite_proof records were provided.
- Whether the PLAUSIBLE vote-for-city change is intended. It needs the csrftoken cookie, so it may be deliberate.

Not rule breaches but worth knowing:
- cli.main now maps any KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError or ValueError to ContractBroken (exit 14). An ordinary program bug would then show up as "the site changed", and the skill would tell the user to rediscover the site.
- Bare HH:MM now rolls to tomorrow once it is more than 15 minutes past. The input is the same but its meaning changed.
- plan.md line 8 still says every command takes --city.
- save-place and create-go-link now require --city at parse time. Before, they already exited 2 at runtime without it, so users see no difference.

One write outside the reviewed files: a PostToolUse slow-command hook asked for a lesson line, so I appended one to ~/.claude/slow-command-lessons.md. I did not touch any reviewed file or test-bound.py.

Next step: you could decide whether the --confirm, --use-web-session-id, plan-cab flag and adopt-session --stdin changes should stay as deliberate breaks or be made backward compatible.
